extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO disciplinary officers, and attorneys subject to USPTO regulation
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements governing approval of an Affidavit of Resignation and exclusion on consent from practice before the USPTO, and the professional-conduct rules alleged violated in the underlying disciplinary complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of Resignation compliance (37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's Affidavit of Resignation must comply with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By approving the Affidavit the Director determined it complied with § 11.27(a). The document indicates the affidavit should show competency, that consent is freely and voluntarily rendered (no coercion/duress), awareness of pending disciplinary complaints and allegations, acknowledgment of the legal consequences of consenting to exclusion, and an explicit consent to be excluded from practice before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary and competent consent to exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must acknowledge he is competent and that his consent to resign/exclude is freely and voluntarily rendered and not the result of coercion or duress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit should state competence and voluntariness (the Order quotes Respondent's acknowledgement as element 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of pending disciplinary complaint and allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must acknowledge awareness of any disciplinary complaint pending against him and the allegations contained therein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit here explicitly states Respondent was aware of Proceeding No. D2016-32 and the detailed allegations (unauthorized practice, failure to supervise, excessive fees, false statements, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge of relevant regulations and consequences (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.27, 11.58, 11.59, 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must state that he has fully read and understands 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.27, 11.58, 11.59, and 11.60 and is aware of the legal and factual consequences of consenting to exclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit should demonstrate informed consent by acknowledging these specific regulatory provisions and consequences, as item 6 in the affidavit does.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent to exclusion from practice before USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must expressly consent to being excluded from practice before the USPTO in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit must include an explicit statement of consent to exclusion (item 7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption on reinstatement (37 C.F.R. § 11.60 effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: If and when the excluded practitioner applies for reinstatement, the OED Director will conclusively presume, for the purpose of determining the reinstatement application, that the allegations in the complaint are true and that the practitioner could not have successfully defended against them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit should acknowledge this conclusive presumption; Respondent here agreed that OED Director will presume allegations true when evaluating any future reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's authority to approve affidavit and exclude (35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32; 37 C.F.R. § 11.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has statutory and regulatory authority to approve an Affidavit of Resignation and to order exclusion on consent from practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This order cites 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.27 as the legal basis for approving resignations and ordering exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order (OED FOIA Reading Room and Official Gazette)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order in the OED FOIA Reading Room and shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural requirement: the order directs publication locations and provides text for a notice of exclusion on consent to be used in the Official Gazette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 (duties following resignation/exclusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order requirement: excluded practitioner must follow the obligations set out in § 11.58 (e.g., notification and handling of pending matters), as stated in the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order requires adherence to the reinstatement procedural and substantive standards set out in § 11.60 when applying to return to practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(a): engaging in disreputable or gross misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Alleged violation: engaging in disreputable or gross misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited as one of the alleged grounds for discipline in the complaint; the order lists it verbatim as a charged rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4): conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Alleged violation: engaging in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed among the Code of Professional Responsibility provisions alleged to have been violated.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5): conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice
rubrics_metrics.description: Alleged violation: engaging in conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed in the complaint as an asserted basis for discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6): other acts adversely reflecting on fitness to practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Alleged violation: engaging in acts that adversely reflect on a practitioner's fitness to practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited as a charged rule for alleged misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.36: entering into, charging, and collecting an illegal or clearly excessive fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Alleged violation: entering into an agreement for, charging, and collecting an illegal or clearly excessive fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complaint alleges Respondent charged clearly excessive fees (e.g., taking advanced fees for mortgage modification services and not performing).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.47(c): aiding a non-lawyer in the unauthorized practice of law
rubrics_metrics.description: Alleged violation: aiding a non-lawyer in the unauthorized practice of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegation includes allowing/authorizing non-lawyer assistants to prepare and file trademark and patent documents and to provide legal advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(b): handling a legal matter without adequate preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Alleged violation: handling a legal matter without preparation adequate in the circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complaint asserts Respondent failed to personally prepare for and advise on matters, delegating to unqualified assistants.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c): neglecting legal matters entrusted to the practitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: Alleged violation: neglecting legal matters entrusted to the practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations include neglect of mortgage modification matters causing client property loss and failure to return unearned fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.84(a)(1)-(3): failing to represent a client zealously
rubrics_metrics.description: Alleged violation: failing to represent a client zealously (subparts (1), (2), and (3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a charged provision; factual allegations include failure to counsel clients directly or explain basic patent/trademark concepts.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.85(a)(5): knowingly making a false statement of law or fact in representing a client
rubrics_metrics.description: Alleged violation: in representing a client, knowingly making a false statement of law or fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complaint alleges false and misleading statements to clients about status of matters and false claims about licensure.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.112(a) and (c)(4): failing to preserve identity of funds and property of a client
rubrics_metrics.description: Alleged violation: failing to preserve identity of client funds and property (including improper handling of advance fees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations include not depositing advanced fees into trust, not returning unearned fees, and mismanagement of client funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.101: failing to provide competent representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Alleged violation under the Rules of Professional Conduct: failing to provide competent representation to a client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complaint alleges Respondent failed to personally provide patent/trademark legal advice and allowed unqualified assistants to advise clients.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.103: failing to act with reasonable diligence and promptness
rubrics_metrics.description: Alleged violation: failing to act with reasonable diligence and promptness in representing a client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations include neglecting mortgage modification matters and failing to timely handle other client matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(3)-(5): failing to keep clients informed and consult on limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Alleged violation: failing to keep clients reasonably informed about the status of a matter, failing to promptly comply with reasonable requests for information, and failing to consult about relevant limitations when the client expects assistance not permitted by rules or law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent is alleged not to have counseled clients directly or responded to client requests for information.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.105(a): making an agreement for, and collecting, an unreasonable fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Alleged violation: making an agreement for, and collecting, an unreasonable fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complaint alleges clearly excessive fees for mortgage modification services and taking advanced unearned fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.115(a): failing to hold client property separate from practitioner's property
rubrics_metrics.description: Alleged violation: failing to hold property of clients in the practitioner's possession separate from the practitioner's own property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Related to mishandling of client funds and advance fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.115(c): failing to deposit advance payments into client trust account
rubrics_metrics.description: Alleged violation: failing to deposit funds received to secure payment of legal fees paid in advance into a client trust account, to be withdrawn only as fees are incurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complaint asserts advanced fees were not properly deposited and maintained in trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.304(c): knowingly disobeying obligations under rules of a tribunal
rubrics_metrics.description: Alleged violation: knowingly disobeying an obligation under the rules of a tribunal by violating multiple court and state agency orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order cites multiple state orders (CT, WA, IN) that Respondent allegedly violated or failed to comply with and for which penalties remain unpaid.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.503: failing to make reasonable efforts to ensure non-attorney conduct is compatible with professional obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Alleged violation: failing, as a partner in a law firm, to make reasonable efforts to ensure the firm has measures assuring non-attorney assistants' conduct is compatible with professional obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations include allowing and directing non-lawyer assistants to prepare documents, forge signatures, file applications, and provide legal advice without proper supervision or guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.505: aiding in the unauthorized practice of law
rubrics_metrics.description: Alleged violation: aiding in the unauthorized practice of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complaint alleges Respondent allowed non-lawyer assistants to practice law and to act on matters while Respondent was suspended.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.701: making a false or misleading communication about the practitioner or services
rubrics_metrics.description: Alleged violation: making a false or misleading communication about the practitioner or the practitioner's services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations include falsely stating licensure in other jurisdictions and misrepresenting the status of client matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.801(b): failing to cooperate with OED and failing to respond to lawful demands
rubrics_metrics.description: Alleged violation: failing to cooperate with the Office of Enrollment and Discipline in an investigation and knowingly failing to respond to a lawful demand for information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent did not fully respond to OED's first request and did not respond to the second request for information.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(c): engaging in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit or misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Alleged violation: engaging in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit or misrepresentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed among the alleged Rules violations; factual allegations include forgery of signature and false statements to clients.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(d): engaging in conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice
rubrics_metrics.description: Alleged violation: engaging in conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited as a charged violation reflecting serious professional misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(i): other acts adversely reflecting on fitness to practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Alleged violation: engaging in other acts that adversely reflect on a practitioner's fitness to practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catch-all provision cited to cover other alleged adverse-conduct aspects not covered by specific rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unauthorized practice while suspended; misrepresentations about licensure and jurisdictional practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Allegations that Respondent practiced in jurisdictions where he was not admitted (e.g., Connecticut, Washington, Indiana) and falsely stated he was licensed to practice in jurisdictions other than Pennsylvania.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order recounts state agency orders and penalties from CT, WA, and IN for unauthorized practice and related conduct; nonpayment of civil penalties is noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation and forgery by non-lawyer assistants (failure of supervision and misrepresentation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Allegations that Respondent allowed and directed non-lawyer assistants to prepare and file trademark and patent documents, electronically forge Respondent's name, and directly counsel clients without adequate supervision or disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific examples listed: preparing and filing applications and statements of use, authorizing Examiner's Amendments, and non-lawyer provision of legal advice; cited as violating supervision and unauthorized-practice rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taking advanced/unearned fees and failing to return them; threats to clients
rubrics_metrics.description: Allegations that Respondent took advanced fees for mortgage modification services, charged clearly excessive fees, did not perform the services, failed to return unearned fees when requested, and in some instances threatened clients seeking refunds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These conduct allegations are tied to rules about unreasonable/excessive fees and mishandling of client funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neglect and failure to counsel clients (failure to provide basic legal advice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Allegations that Respondent failed to personally counsel clients or explain basic patent/trademark concepts, leaving clients to deal only with non-lawyer assistants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These facts are cited in support of charges for lack of competent representation, lack of diligence, and failure to keep clients informed.
